sections.text:
In a small, beautiful Italian town, there was an old, kind-hearted carpenter named “Geppetto” (or Geppetto), who lived alone after he had grown old without having a child.

Geppetto was very skilled at making wooden toys and music boxes, and one day, he obtained a special piece of pine wood from a nearby forest.

Geppetto decided to make a moving wooden doll in the shape of a boy from this piece, and he carved it with love and care, and called it “Pinocchio.”

While he was sculpting the doll, he was surprised that it responded to him: the nose became longer, and the eyes moved! When he finished making it, he looked at it and sighed, saying: “I wish with all my heart that I were a real boy to fill my life.”

That night, while Geppetto was sleeping, the good Blue Fairy descended into his workshop and heard his sincere wish.

The fairy waved her magic wand over the doll and said: “Pinocchio, I give you life, but in order to become a real human boy, you must prove that you are brave, honest, and loyal, and listen to the voice of your conscience.”

The Blue Fairy appointed a small and intelligent cricket named “Jimini” to be Pinocchio’s conscience and his guide in making the right decisions.

The next morning, Geppetto woke up to find that his wooden doll was moving, talking, and calling him, “Dad!” His heart was filled with joy and he cried with happiness.

Geppetto sold his only coat to buy a textbook for Pinocchio, and the next morning he sent him to school to learn and be a good boy.

On his way to school, Pinocchio met a cunning fox and a deceitful cat, who convinced him that going to school was a waste of time, and that he should go with them to the puppet theater to be a star and get a lot of money for his father.

Pinocchio forgot his father's advice and ignored the warnings of his cricket, Jiminy, and went with them, but the evil theater manager locked him in a cage to exploit him in performances!
The Blue Fairy appeared to save him, and asked him why he did not go to school, so Pinocchio began making up lies and making up stories.

With every lie he told, his wooden nose grew longer and longer until it hit the wall of the cage!
The fairy said: “A lie is not hidden, Pinocchio. It appears as a long nose that everyone can see.”

Pinocchio apologized and cried, so the fairy restored his nose to its normal size and saved him, and he promised to be obedient.

But Pinocchio was a naive and easily deceived child, so he was soon tricked again by a gang of naughty boys into going to the “Island of Fun”, where they played all day, no schools, and no obligations.

On that island, children who disobeyed their parents were gradually turned into donkeys to be sold in the mines!
Pinocchio's ears began to lengthen like a donkey's ears, and a tail grew, so he realized the grave mistake he had committed, and escaped with difficulty with his friend "Gimini" before he was completely transformed.

Pinocchio quickly returned home to apologize to his father, but he found the house completely empty.

He discovered from a small letter that his father, Geppetto, was deeply saddened by his absence, so he made a small boat and went out to search for him in the sea, but a giant and terrifying whale called “Monstro” swallowed him!
Pinocchio did not hesitate for a single moment, so he ran towards the beach, tied a rock to his feet, and dived into the depths of the dark ocean to search for his father to save him.

He faced sharks and strong currents until he found the giant whale sleeping, so he allowed himself to be swallowed by the whale along with the water current.

In the dark belly of the whale, he found his father, Geppetto, hungry and sad, so they embraced each other with joy and tears.

To get out of the belly of the whale, Pinocchio prepared a very clever plan. He collected the broken wood inside the whale and lit a big fire.

The thick smoke made the whale suffocate and sneeze with great force, and the sneezing threw them far out of the sea onto a wooden raft.

But the angry whale woke up and started chasing the raft to destroy it, and at the last moment, Pinocchio sacrificed himself and jumped to push his father towards the shore to save him from the whale's teeth.

When Geppetto woke up on the beach, he found the wooden Pinocchio lying next to him, lifeless due to the force of the impact.

The father carried his doll and returned home crying bitterly, and placed it on the bed praying to God to return it to him.

At that moment, the Blue Fairy appeared again and said: “Pinocchio, you have proven that you are very brave, honest, and loyal to your father to the point of sacrificing your life.”

With a touch of her wand, Pinocchio's hardened wooden body was transformed into soft, warm human flesh and blood!
Pinocchio woke up to find himself a real boy, as he and his father always wished, and Geppetto and his son lived very happily, and Pinocchio never lied after that.
